stemMd: Which statement cannot be true in any permitted order?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Iris must not be in position 4.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Rose and Iris must not occupy consecutive positions.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Rose and Iris must occupy consecutive positions, in either order.

explanationMd:
Test whether each proposed statement can be added consistently to the rules. "Iris must not be in position 4." is incompatible with every permitted order. The alternative statements each have a complete valid example, given in their feedback. To check impossibility, enumerate placements for the most restricted item or block, then remove every case breaking a rule.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Dahlia → Aster → Rose → Iris → Lily
- Lily → Aster → Rose → Iris → Dahlia
- Rose → Aster → Dahlia → Iris → Lily
- Rose → Aster → Lily → Iris → Dahlia

distractorRationale.a: This is possible, as demonstrated by Dahlia → Aster → Rose → Iris → Lily, which obeys all the original conditions.
distractorRationale.d: This is possible, as demonstrated by Dahlia → Aster → Rose → Iris → Lily, which obeys all the original conditions.
distractorRationale.c: This is possible, as demonstrated by Rose → Aster → Dahlia → Iris → Lily, which obeys all the original conditions.

Iris must not be in position 5. leave 4 valid orders: Dahlia>Aster>Rose>Iris>Lily; Lily>Aster>Rose>Iris>Dahlia; Rose>Aster>Dahlia>Iris>Lily; Rose>Aster>Lily>Iris>Dahlia. Choice true counts: a=3, b=0, c=2, d=2; impossible requires zero matches.
